questions.question: What are the two inputs of scalar multiplication?
options: Two vectors.
Two scalars only.
A matrix and a determinant only.
A scalar and a vector.

questions.question: What is the output of $\alpha v$?
options: A statement rather than an object.
A field.
A scalar in $\mathbb F$.
A vector in $V$.

questions.question: What does multiplying a vector by a negative scalar often do geometrically?
options: It makes the vector undefined.
It reverses direction as well as scaling length.
It always gives the zero vector.
It turns the vector into a scalar, which is false

questions.question: What does the rule $1v=v$ say?
options: Only the zero vector can be multiplied by $1$.
$1v$ is always the zero vector.
The scalar $1$ leaves every vector unchanged.
Every vector is equal to the scalar $1$.

questions.question: What does $(\alpha\beta)v=\alpha(\beta v)$ allow you to do?
options: Conclude that all scalars are equal
Replace every scalar by a vector.
Add two unrelated vector spaces.
Group successive scalar multiplications

questions.question: Compute $-1(3,5)$.
What is $\frac12(6,8)$?
Which expression is scalar multiplication?
options: $V+\mathbb F$
$u+v$
$uv$ for two vectors $u,v$

questions.question: Why is scalar multiplication not the same operation as vector addition?
options: It combines a field element with a vector, not two vectors.
It produces only scalars.
It requires two vectors of the same dimension.
It produces a vector of a different dimension.

questions.question: What does scalar multiplication by a number between $0$ and $1$ usually do to a nonzero vector in Euclidean space?
options: It shrinks the vector without reversing it.
It always makes the vector zero.
It always reverses the vector.
It changes the vector into a scalar.

questions.question: Why does scalar multiplication by $1$ matter as an axiom?
options: It makes the field identity act as identity on vectors
It removes the need for vector addition.
It makes all nonzero vectors have length $1$
It makes every vector equal to $1$.

questions.question: Which expression equals $(\alpha\beta)v$ by the scalar multiplication rule?
options: $\alpha+\beta+v$
$\alpha(\beta v)$
$\beta(\alpha+v)$
$(\alpha v)(\beta v)$

questions.question: Why does the scalar field matter in scalar multiplication?
options: Every vector space allows all possible mathematical objects as scalars.
The scalar must come from the field over which $V$ is defined.
The scalar field determines the number of vectors in $V$ only.
Scalar multiplication ignores the field.

questions.question: If $\alpha v=\boldsymbol0$, is it always necessary that $v=\boldsymbol0$?
options: Yes, the scalar never matters.
No; it can happen for any nonzero scalar and any nonzero vector.
No; it could also happen because $\alpha=0$.
Yes, unless the vector has two coordinates.

questions.question: Find $a$ such that $a(2,-4)=(1,-2)$.
options: No such scalar exists.
$a=\frac12$
